about: Swiss dermatology company producing injectable aesthetics (Restylane, Dysport, Sculptra), dermatological skincare (Cetaphil, Differin, Benzac) and prescription treatments. Customers are dermatologists, healthcare professionals and consumers through pharmacies, with sales near 4 to 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland; operations in 90 countries. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (GALD) after a 2024 IPO, with EQT and ADIA as leading shareholders. Cetaphil is a widely recognised consumer skincare brand.

wiki.title: Galderma
wiki.text: Galderma S.A. is a Swiss pharmaceutical company based in Zug that specializes in dermatological treatments and skin care products. Formerly a subsidiary of L'Oréal and Nestlé, it was acquired by a consortium of private institutional investors in 2019 and remained under their ownership until its initial public offering in 2024. It has been a component of the Swiss Market Index since September 2026.

about: Online retail and technology group owning beauty brands (LookFantastic, Cult Beauty, Dermstore), nutrition (Myprotein, Myvegan), and the THG Ingenuity technology platform that powers e-commerce for other brands. Customers are consumers in 160-plus countries and brand partners, with revenue near 2 billion pounds. Headquartered in Manchester, England; founded 2004 by Matthew Moulding as The Hut Group. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (THG) since 2020. Myprotein and LookFantastic are strong consumer brands, with sports and athlete partnerships.

dsm-firmenich is a Dutch-Swiss company, created in 2023 by the merger of DSM and Firmenich, producing flavours, fragrances, nutritional ingredients, vitamins and health and beauty ingredients. It sells to food and drink, perfume, personal care, pharma and animal feed makers worldwide, with annual revenue around EUR 12bn and about 28,000 staff. Its animal nutrition business is being divested. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (DSFIR), with offices in Kaiseraugst and Maastricht. B2B ingredient supplier; consumers rarely see the brand, though customers include major consumer brands.

Valentino is a Milan-based Italian luxury fashion house, founded in 1960 in Rome by Valentino Garavani and Giancarlo Giammetti, selling ready-to-wear, accessories, shoes, beauty and fragrance through boutiques, department stores and e-commerce worldwide, with revenue near EUR 1.4bn. Qatar's Mayhoola owns it, and Kering agreed in 2023 to buy a 30 percent stake, rising to full ownership by 2028. Private. Globally recognised luxury brand, with the red Valentino colour as an asset; limited sports ties.

Debenhams Group is a UK online fashion and beauty marketplace company, the successor of the former Boohoo Group, which renamed itself in 2025 and operates Debenhams.com, Karen Millen, Coast, Warehouse and boohoo brands. Based in Manchester. The input shows 116.5 million reported funding. Listed on AIM in London (DEBS). Consumers are shoppers in the UK and abroad. The Debenhams brand, once a department store, is widely known in Britain.
cb_desc: The aim of the Debenhams Group is to maximize value for...

wiki.title: Debenhams Group
wiki.text: Boohoo Group plc, trading as Debenhams Group, is an online retail platform that operates five core brands, Debenhams, Karen Millen, boohoo, boohooMAN, and PrettyLittleThing, in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle retail.

about: Nykaa (FSN E-Commerce Ventures) is an Indian beauty, personal care and fashion retailer headquartered in Mumbai and listed on the NSE and BSE since 2021. It runs the Nykaa app and website, Nykaa Fashion, and hundreds of physical stores, plus own brands such as Kay Beauty and Dot and Key, selling to millions of consumers. Founded 2012 by Falguni Nayar. Revenue exceeds 70 billion rupees. Strong consumer brand with young women and heavy celebrity and sports marketing.

wiki.title: Nykaa
wiki.text: FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd, doing business as Nykaa, is an Indian retail company, headquartered in Mumbai. It sells beauty, wellness and fashion products online and through physical stores. It also operates an eB2B distribution business called Superstore by Nykaa.

about: Wella Company is a global beauty company based in Woodland Hills, California with major operations in Germany and Switzerland, whose brands include Wella Professionals, Clairol, OPI, Nioxin, Sebastian Professional and ghd. It sells hair colour, care, styling and nail products to salons, retailers and consumers in over 100 countries. It was acquired by Coty in 2016 and majority-sold to KKR in 2020, with Coty retaining a minority stake. Strong professional and consumer beauty brands worldwide.

wiki.title: Wella
wiki.text: Wella is a multinational hair care and cosmetics company headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. It develops, manufactures, and distributes professional and consumer hair and nail products, including coloring, styling, and hair care lines. Founded in 1880 in Germany by Franz Ströher, the company has undergone multiple ownership transitions. Since 2020, it has operated as an independent entity, majority-owned by private equity firm KKR following its separation from Coty Inc.

about: Bath & Body Works is a specialty retailer of fragrances and personal care: body care, fine fragrance mist, hand soaps and sanitisers, 3-wick candles and home fragrance, sold under Bath & Body Works and White Barn brands. Customers are mainly women shopping in about 1,900 US and Canadian mall and street stores, plus online and international franchise stores. Revenue is around $7 billion. Headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, spun out of L Brands in 2021. Listed on NYSE (BBWI). Very strong consumer brand awareness in North America.

wiki.title: Bath & Body Works
wiki.text: Bath & Body Works, LLC. is an American retail store chain that sells soaps, lotions, fragrances, candles, accessories, and hand sanitizers. It was founded in 1990 in New Albany, Ohio, and has since expanded across six continents. In 1997, it became the largest bath shop chain in the United States.

about: Tiendas 3B is a Mexican retail chain that, according to Crunchbase, offers household cleaning, personal hygiene, food and beverage and other everyday products. It is listed with a location in Colima, Mexico, and is classified under cosmetics and food and beverage. Crunchbase shows about $1.03 billion in funding, likely corporate or debt financing. Store count, ownership and revenue are not stated in the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Tiendas 3B offers household cleaning, personal hygiene,..

about: Growve is a St. Petersburg, Florida-based consumer brand aggregator in beauty and personal care, which acquires and scales online brands. The input shows funding of about $400 million. Specific brands and scale are not confirmed. The input shows its work in beauty and brand marketing, and it appears to own a portfolio of consumer products sold online. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Growve is abrand aggregator that specializes in the...

about: Yatsen Holding is a Chinese beauty group behind Perfect Diary, Little Ondine, Abby's Choice, Galenic and DR.WU, selling cosmetics and skincare mainly through online channels such as Tmall, Douyin and its own stores. Founded in 2016 and based in Guangzhou, it listed on the NYSE (YSG) in 2020. Revenue is around 4 billion yuan, down from peak levels, as competition in Chinese beauty has intensified. Perfect Diary is a prominent consumer brand with celebrity endorsements in China.

Glossier is a New York direct-to-consumer beauty brand founded by Emily Weiss in 2014 from the Into The Gloss blog, selling minimalist skincare and make-up such as Boy Brow, Cloud Paint and Balm Dotcom online, in its own stores and, from 2022, through Sephora. Customers are mainly young women, and it is known for community-driven marketing. It raised over 300 million dollars at a valuation of 1.8 billion dollars in 2019. Weiss stepped back in 2022 and Kyle Leahy became CEO. Strong consumer brand with a loyal following.

wiki.title: Glossier
wiki.text: Glossier is an American beauty company founded by Emily Weiss in 2014. It originated as an online-only business, building on Weiss's beauty blog, Into the Gloss. Later, it expanded into pop-up shops and retail locations. It distributes its products through its website, select retail locations, and stores such as Sephora, SpaceNK, and Mecca.

about: US beauty company founded in 1932 and based in New York, selling cosmetics, nail polish, hair colour and fragrance under Revlon, Almay, Elizabeth Arden and Elizabeth Taylor lines, mass-market through retailers worldwide. Filed for Chapter 11 in 2022 and emerged in 2023 as a private company owned by its lenders. Revenue is roughly USD 1.9 billion. Consumer brand sold in many countries with very high awareness.

wiki.title: Revlon
wiki.text: Revlon, Inc., is an American multinational company dealing in cosmetics, skin care, perfume, and personal care. The headquarters of Revlon was established in New York City on March 1, 1932, where it remains. Revlon was founded by brothers Charles and Joseph Revson, and chemist Charles Lachman. Revlon products are sold in 150 countries and the company has many global locations including Mexico City, London, Paris, Hong Kong, Indonesia, South Africa, Sydney, Singapore, and Tokyo.

about: San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer hair colour company founded 2013, selling at-home hair colour kits, care and root touch-up products online and through retailers such as Target and Ulta, plus salons in several US cities. Has raised roughly USD 313 million. Consumer brand with national US awareness and heavy digital marketing.

wiki.title: Madison Reed
wiki.what: American brand of natural hair care and hair color products
wiki.text: Madison Reed is an American brand of hair care and hair color products. The company has a subscription-based service through its online and brick-and-mortar stores as well as retail partnerships with Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Sally Beauty, and Amazon.com. The company also operates brick-and-mortar "Hair Color Bars" in cities across the United States. A class action suit with allegations that included hair damage, hair loss, false advertising, and use of known carcinogen ethanolamine presented as a "natural" alternative to the ammonia typically found in hair dye was filed against the company in 2022 and was settled out of court in 2024.

about: Brazilian cosmetics and beauty group, owner of Natura, Avon, The Body Shop and Aesop. Direct-selling model with millions of consultants. Based in Sao Paulo, listed on B3 (NATU3). Now named Natura Cosmeticos, the group sold Aesop to L'Oreal in 2023 and The Body Shop to Aurelius that year. Avon Products went through a US Chapter 11 process in 2024. Strong global consumer brands.
Medical aesthetics company Venus Concept, headquartered in Toronto, selling energy-based body and skin devices to clinics. Listed on Nasdaq (VERO). B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Ulta Beauty is a US specialty beauty retailer based in Bolingbrook, Illinois, with well over 1,400 stores, selling cosmetics, skincare, haircare, fragrance and salon services from hundreds of brands, plus its own Ulta Beauty Collection, and an online store. It is the largest US beauty retailer by sales, with revenue above 11 billion dollars, and it is listed on Nasdaq (ULTA). It is a very well known consumer brand and loyalty programme (Ultamate Rewards), with a strong advertising presence.

wiki.title: Ulta Beauty
wiki.text: Ulta Beauty, Inc., formerly known as Ulta Salon, Cosmetics & Fragrance Inc. and before 2000 as Ulta3, is an American chain of cosmetic stores headquartered in Bolingbrook, Illinois. Ulta Beauty carries both high- and low-end cosmetics, fragrances, nail products, bath and body products, beauty tools and haircare products. Nearly every Ulta Beauty store features a full-service salon.

about: Grupo Cimed is a Brazilian pharmaceutical company based in Sao Paulo (originally Pouso Alegre, Minas Gerais), producing generic and branded medicines, over-the-counter products and cosmetics, sold through pharmacies across Brazil. It is privately held by the Pinto family and had a significant presence in the Brazilian consumer healthcare market. The record shows about R$1.3 billion of funding. It is a consumer health brand, known for TV advertising, and sponsors football in Brazil.
cb_desc: Grupo Cimed is a pharmaceutical firm that..

about: AptarGroup is a global maker of dispensing, sealing and active packaging solutions, such as pumps, sprays, closures and drug delivery devices, for beauty, personal care, pharma, food and beverage and home care customers. It supplies brands like major cosmetics and pharmaceutical firms across about 20 countries with about 14,000 employees and revenue near 3.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Crystal Lake, Illinois, and listed on the NYSE (ATR). B2B supplier whose products are in many everyday items, but with no consumer name recognition.

wiki.title: AptarGroup
wiki.text: AptarGroup, Inc., also known as Aptar, is a United States–based global manufacturer of consumer dispensing packaging and drug delivery devices. The group has manufacturing operations in 18 countries.

about: European Wax Center is a US franchisor of waxing salons, with over 1,000 centres across the country offering hair removal services and a retail range of skincare products. Revenue comes from franchise royalties and product sales; system-wide sales approach 1 billion dollars. Founded in 2004 and based in Plano, Texas, it was backed by General Atlantic and listed on Nasdaq in 2021 (EWCZ). Strong US consumer brand in personal care, primarily female customers, with heavy digital marketing.

wiki.title: European Wax Center
wiki.what: American chain of hair removal salons
wiki.text: European Wax Center (EWC) is an American chain of hair-removal centers specializing in professional Waxing services and related skincare products. Founded in Aventura, Florida, in 2004 by siblings Joshua and David Coba, the company is headquartered in Plano, Texas, and operates primarily through franchised locations. As of January 2026, European Wax Center operated 1,047 centers across 44 U.S. states, of which 1,042 were franchise-operated.

about: Regis Corporation is a US hair salon franchisor, with brands including Supercuts, SmartStyle, Cost Cutters and Holiday Hair, which together operate several thousand salons, mostly franchised. It is headquartered in Minneapolis and listed on Nasdaq (RGS). The company sold its company-owned salons and moved to a franchise model, earning royalties and fees. Customers are walk-in consumers, mostly in North America. Supercuts and SmartStyle are well known US consumer brands.

wiki.title: Regis Corporation
wiki.text: Regis Corporation is an American operator of hair salons. As of August 2021, it has 5,563 franchised and 276 company-owned salons. Its headquarters are in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

about: Sono Bello is a Bellevue, Washington cosmetic surgery company that offers laser liposuction, body contouring and other cosmetic procedures through dozens of centres in the US, using a consumer-financing model. It is privately owned, and it advertises heavily on television. Customers are consumers paying for elective procedures. Funding of about $611 million is shown. Strong awareness among US TV audiences, though cosmetic surgery is a niche sponsorship category.
cb_desc: Sono Bello is a medical practice specializing in laser liposucti..

about: Lindex Group is a Nordic fashion retailer headquartered in Helsinki (operations originally in Gothenburg, Sweden), selling women's, children's and lingerie clothing and beauty products through roughly 400 stores and an online shop across Sweden, Norway, Finland, the Baltics and other markets. It was owned by the Finnish retailer Stockmann until 2019, when it was sold to Finnish investors, and it listed on Nasdaq Helsinki in 2024. A well-known consumer brand in Scandinavia, which suits sponsorship.

International handmade cosmetics retailer, famed for fresh bath bombs, soaps and skincare sold in about 900 shops in 50 countries. Founded in Poole, England in 1995, with its Canadian subsidiary in Vancouver. Privately owned by its founders. Strong ethical and consumer brand recognition, with campaigns on animal testing and sustainability.

Thrive Market is a US membership-based online grocer, based in Los Angeles, founded in 2014 by Nick Green and Gunnar Lovelace, selling organic, natural and non-GMO groceries, household items and beauty products at discounted prices to members who pay an annual fee. It also has private-label Thrive Market products. It raised about $243 million. Customers are health-conscious US households. Well-known niche consumer brand with heavy digital marketing.

wiki.title: Thrive Market
wiki.text: Thrive Market is an American e-commerce membership-based retailer offering natural and organic food products. It was founded by Nick Green, Gunnar Lovelace, Kate Mulling, and Sasha Siddhartha. By 2016 they had raised $141 million across three funding rounds following their launch in November 2014.

wiki.title: Moody's Corporation
wiki.what: American business and financial services company
wiki.text: Moody's Corporation is an American business and financial services company. It is the holding company for Moody's Ratings, an American credit rating agency, and Moody's, an American provider of financial analysis software and services.

about: MAV Beauty Brands is described in the input as a high-growth global personal care company based in Vaughan, Ontario, Canada, operating in beauty and cosmetics. It owns and sells a portfolio of beauty and personal care brands through retailers and online channels. Crunchbase shows about C$230 million of funding in November 2016, which suggests institutional backing. The input does not name the individual brands, revenue or owners. Consumer-product company whose corporate name is little known. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: MAV Beauty Brands is a high- growth global personal care..

about: Pacific World Corporation is a beauty and consumer goods company based in Glendale, California, tagged in Crunchbase under beauty and consumer goods. The description calls it an innovator and supplier of products, but the text is cut off, so its brands, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the input. It likely supplies personal care items to retailers. Funding of about 215 million dollars is shown. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Pacific World Corporation is an innovator and supplier of...

about: JCPenney is a US mid-range department store chain selling apparel, home goods and jewellery from about 650 stores and online. Headquartered in Plano, Texas; founded 1902. It went bankrupt in 2020 and was bought out of Chapter 11 by Simon Property Group and Brookfield, then merged with SPARC Group (Aeropostale and Nine West owner) in early 2025 to form Catalyst Brands. Established household brand across the US, particularly in small and mid-size towns.

wiki.title: JCPenney
wiki.text: JCPenney is an American department store chain founded in 1902 by James Cash Penney. It is owned by Catalyst Brands, a joint venture between Authentic Brands Group, Brookfield Corporation, and Simon Property Group, since 2025.

about: Hudson's Bay Company was a Canadian retail group founded in 1670, and one of the oldest companies in North America. It operated Hudson's Bay department stores in Canada, and earlier owned Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord and Taylor, selling fashion, beauty and home goods. After pandemic pressures, the Canadian business sought creditor protection in March 2025 and liquidated, closing all stores by mid-2025. The Saks brands sit in separate Saks Global. Formerly a very recognisable Canadian consumer brand; now defunct as a retailer.

wiki.title: Hudson's Bay Company
wiki.text: The Hudson's Bay Company was a Canadian holding company of department stores and commercial property. It was the oldest commercial corporation in North America, founded in 1670 and liquidated in 2025. It was headquartered at the Simpson Tower in Toronto, becoming an intellectual property and brand of Canadian Tire for its iconic point stripe blankets and other merchandise within Canadian Tire stores.

about: Gildan is a Montreal-based manufacturer of basic apparel, selling T-shirts, fleece, socks, underwear and hosiery under brands such as Gildan, Gold Toe, Comfort Colors, American Apparel and Hanes after buying HanesBrands in a deal announced in 2025. It is vertically integrated, with plants in Central America and the Caribbean, selling mostly to screen printers and wholesale distributors, plus retailers. Revenue is around $3.3bn. Listed on the NYSE and TSX (GIL). Wholesale-focused, so the consumer brand profile is modest apart from its retail sock and underwear brands.

wiki.title: Gildan
wiki.text: Gildan Activewear Inc. is a Canadian manufacturer of branded clothing, including undecorated blank activewear such as t-shirts, hoodies and fleeces, which are subsequently decorated by screen printing companies with designs and logos. The company also supplies branded and private label athletic, casual, and dress socks to retail companies in the United States including Gold Toe Brands, PowerSox, SilverToe, Auro, All Pro, and the Gildan brand. The company also manufactures and distributes Under Armour and New Balance brand socks. The company has approximately 50,000 employees worldwide, and owns and operates manufacturing facilities in Rio Nan

about: Aritzia is a Vancouver-based women's fashion retailer, designing everyday luxury apparel under brands such as Babaton, Wilfred, Sunday Best and TNA, sold through about 130 boutiques in Canada and the US plus online. Revenue is above C$3bn and it has grown fast in the US. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ATZ), with the Chiu family and Berkshire Partners investor in the past. Strong consumer fashion brand in Canada, with growing US awareness.

wiki.title: Aritzia
wiki.text: Aritzia LP is a Canadian clothing retail company founded in Vancouver, British Columbia, by businessman Brian Hill in 1984. Aritzia sells a variety of lifestyle apparel through various upscale retail stores across Canada, the United States, and online. Aritzia describes itself as an "everyday luxury" brand at attainable prices. The company has targeted $10.5 billion dollars in annual revenue by 2032.

wiki.title: Transitions Optical
wiki.text: Transitions Optical is a U.S.-based company known for manufacturing photochromic lenses, which darken on exposure to specific types of light. The company was founded in 1990 as a joint venture between PPG Industries (51%) and Essilor (49%). In April 2014, Essilor acquired PPG's entire stake in Transitions, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary. After Essilor's merger with Luxottica, it became a subsidiary of the combined EssilorLuxottica.

about: Miniso is a Guangzhou, China-based lifestyle products retailer founded in 2013 by Ye Guofu, selling affordable home goods, accessories, toys and cosmetics with design-led branding and Japanese-style positioning. It has over 7,000 stores in about 100 countries, mostly franchised, including licensed IP collections such as Sanrio and Disney. Listed on the NYSE (MNSO) and in Hong Kong (9896). High consumer awareness in Asia and growing in Western markets.

wiki.title: MINISO
wiki.text: MINISO Group Holding Limited, trading as MINISO is a Chinese retailer and variety store chain that specializes in household and consumer goods including cosmetics, stationery, toys, and kitchenware featuring IP design. Founded in 2013 by Ye Guofu, its headquarters are in Haizhu District, Guangzhou. In 2025, the company's sales revenue reached $2.45 billion.

about: Rent the Runway is a New York online fashion rental platform founded in 2009 by Jennifer Hyman and Jennifer Fleiss, letting customers rent designer dresses and clothing by subscription or per item, with some resale. It is based in New York with distribution hubs in the US and a few retail locations. It listed on Nasdaq (RENT) in 2021; revenue is about $300 million. Strong brand among US women, well-known for fashion marketing.

wiki.title: Rent the Runway
wiki.what: Online service that provides designer dress and accessory rentals
wiki.text: Rent the Runway is an American e-commerce platform that allows users to rent, subscribe, or buy designer apparel and accessories. It was founded in November 2009 by Jennifer Hyman and Jennifer Fleiss and is based in New York City.

about: VF Corporation is a US apparel and footwear company headquartered in Denver, Colorado and listed on the NYSE (VFC). Its brands include The North Face, Vans, Timberland, Dickies, Kipling and Eastpak; the Supreme streetwear brand was sold in 2024. It sells through wholesale, its own stores and e-commerce in about 100 countries, with revenue near 10 billion dollars. Founded 1899 as Vanity Fair Mills. Customers are consumers in outdoor, active and workwear segments. Highly visible consumer brands with strong action-sports and outdoor marketing.

Warby Parker is a US eyewear company headquartered in New York and listed on the NYSE (WRBY), selling prescription glasses, sunglasses and contact lenses through about 300 retail stores and online, with home try-on and an eye exam offering. Customers are mainstream consumers, with revenue near 800 million dollars. Founded 2010 with a buy-a-pair give-a-pair model. Strong direct-to-consumer lifestyle brand among younger consumers.

wiki.title: Warby Parker
wiki.what: American eyeglasses and contact lens retailer
wiki.text: Warby Parker Inc. is an American eyewear brand and retailer of prescription glasses, contact lenses, and sunglasses, headquartered in New York City. It also offers eye exams. Originally founded in 2010 as an online-only retailer, the company now generates most of its revenue from its physical retail stores.

about: Coupang is a South Korean e-commerce giant based in Seattle that runs the Coupang marketplace, Rocket Delivery fast shipping, Rocket Wow membership, Coupang Eats food delivery, Coupang Play streaming and Taiwan expansion, with revenue of around $30 billion and tens of millions of customers. Founded in 2010 by Bom Kim. Listed on NYSE (CPNG) since 2021, with SoftBank Vision Fund a major early investor. Dominant Korean consumer brand with heavy advertising.

wiki.title: Coupang
wiki.text: Coupang, Inc. is an American online retail and technology company headquartered in Seattle, Washington, operating primarily in South Korea and Taiwan. Founded in South Korea in 2010 by Bom Kim and listed on the Fortune 500 as of 2025, Coupang operates an internet retail business, food delivery service, and OTT streaming service. Originally headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, Coupang has offices in South Korea, Taiwan, the United States, India, Japan and Singapore.

about: US department store retailer headquartered in Seattle, founded 1901, selling fashion, beauty and homeware through about 360 Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack stores and online. Revenue is about $15 billion. Taken private in 2025 by the Nordstrom family and Mexico's Liverpool. Strong consumer brand in the US and Canada. Nordstrom has about 60,000 employees, including its off-price Nordstrom Rack stores and the Trunk Club brand.

wiki.title: Nordstrom
wiki.text: Nordstrom, Inc. is an American upmarket department store chain headquartered in Seattle, Washington, and founded by John W. Nordstrom and Carl F. Wallin in 1901. The original store operated exclusively as a shoe store, and a second location opened in 1923. The growing chain began selling clothing in 1963, and became the full-line retailer that presently exists by 1971. The company founded its off-price Nordstrom Rack division in 1973, and grew both full-line and off-price divisions throughout the United States in the following years. The full-line division competes with department stores including Bloomingdale's, Dillard's, Neiman Marcus, and

about: BVI Medical is a manufacturer and marketer of specialised ophthalmic surgical devices, including cataract and retinal surgery instruments, intraocular lenses and glaucoma implants, sold to surgeons and hospitals worldwide. Headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, it grew out of Beaver-Visitec International and is privately held and owned by private equity investors. B2B medical products with no consumer visibility; very limited sponsorship fit.
cb_desc: BVI Medical is a manufacturer, and marketer of specialized....

about: Milan-based Italian luxury group founded in 1910, making menswear and tailoring under the Zegna brand, Thom Browne and Tom Ford Fashion. Sells through its own stores, wholesale and e-commerce worldwide, with revenue of around EUR 1.9 billion. Listed on the NYSE (ZGN) since 2021 after a SPAC merger; the Zegna family controls it. Strong luxury consumer brand, sells in about 80 markets.

wiki.title: Zegna
wiki.text: Ermenegildo Zegna N.V., also known as Zegna Group, Ermenegildo Zegna Group, or simply Zegna, is an Italian luxury fashion house headquartered in Milan. It was founded in 1910 by Ermenegildo Zegna in Trivero, Biella, in the Piedmont region of northern Italy. It is led by the Zegna family and is a public company that is listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

about: Toronto-based luxury outdoor apparel maker famous for down-filled parkas. Designs and sells cold-weather jackets and apparel through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale in more than 50 countries, with revenue about CAD 1.3 billion. Listed on NYSE and TSX (GOOS), controlled by Bain Capital. Premium consumer brand with high awareness and fashion and celebrity presence.

wiki.title: Canada goose
wiki.what: Species of goose native to the Northern Hemisphere
wiki.text: The Canada goose is a large species of goose with a black head and neck, white cheeks, white under its chin, and a brown body. It is native to the Arctic and temperate regions of North America, and it is occasionally found during migration across the Atlantic in northern Europe. It has been introduced to France, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Scandinavia, New Zealand, Japan, Chile, Argentina, and the Falkland Islands. Like most geese, the Canada goose is primarily herbivorous and normally migratory; often found on or close to fresh water, the Canada goose is also common in brackish marshes, estuaries, and lagoons.

wiki.title: Canada Goose Inc.
wiki.text: Canada Goose Inc. is a Canadian holding company of winter clothing manufacturers. The company was founded in 1957 by Sam Tick, under the name Metro Sportswear Ltd. The CEO of Canada Goose is Dani Reiss.

about: Farfetch is a London-based online luxury fashion marketplace, founded in 2007 by Jose Neves, connecting boutiques and brands with consumers in about 190 countries and owning Browns, Stadium Goods and New Guards (Off-White). Coupang acquired it in a rescue deal in 2024 after it struggled and was delisted from the NYSE. Strong luxury consumer brand with sports and fashion collaborations.

wiki.title: Farfetch
wiki.text: Farfetch is a global luxury marketplace headquartered in London. It operates as a digital marketplace that sells products from over 1,400 brands, boutiques and department stores from around the world. In January 2024, the company was acquired by Coupang, a U.S. technology and Fortune 150 company, headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

about: Dolce & Gabbana is an Italian luxury fashion house founded in 1985 in Milan by Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana. It sells ready-to-wear, accessories, eyewear, fragrance, beauty and jewellery through a global store network and e-commerce, with revenue above 1.3 billion euros. It is privately held by its founders. The brand has attracted controversy, including in China in 2018, but remains one of the most recognised luxury names. The record shows funding of about 150 million euros, likely debt.

wiki.title: Dolce & Gabbana
wiki.text: Dolce & Gabbana, also known by initials D&G, is an Italian fashion house founded in 1985 in Legnano by Italian designers Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana. Stefano Gabbana stepped down as chair in December 2025, a decision announced in April 2026, while remaining co-creative director alongside Domenico Dolce. The house specializes in ready-to-wear, haute couture, handbags, accessories, cosmetics, and fragrances and licenses its name and branding to Luxottica for eyewear.

about: Reformation is a US sustainable women's fashion brand, with its corporate base in Los Angeles (the input lists Vernon Hills, Illinois). It sells dresses, tops, denim and shoes through its own stores and online. Founded in 2009, it was acquired by Permira in 2023 and has dozens of stores. Strong consumer brand known for sustainability messaging and celebrity customers.

wiki.title: Reformation
wiki.text: The Reformation, also known as the Protestant Reformation or the European Reformation, was a major theological movement in Western Christianity in 16th-century Europe that posed a religious and political challenge to the papacy and the authority of the Catholic Church hierarchy. Towards the end of the Renaissance, the Reformation marked the beginning of Protestantism. It is considered one of the events that signified the end of the Middle Ages and the beginning of the early modern period in Europe.

about: GOAT Group is a Los Angeles-based online marketplace for sneakers, apparel and accessories, which sells new and pre-owned items from authenticated sellers, and owns Flight Club retail stores. Founded in 2015, it serves tens of millions of members worldwide, with offices in Los Angeles and a large operation in China, and is backed by Matrix Partners, Accel, and Alibaba affiliate-linked investors. It was valued at around 3.7 billion dollars in 2021. Strong brand among sneakerhead consumers.

Mulberry is a British luxury fashion house, founded in 1971 in Somerset, famous for leather handbags such as the Bayswater and Alexa, plus accessories and clothing, made largely at its Somerset factories. It sells through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale. Listed on London AIM, its main shareholders have been Challice (the Christina Ong family) and Frasers Group. Strong luxury brand in the UK and Asia, with a premium customer base.

wiki.title: Mulberry Group
wiki.what: Fashion company founded in England in 1971
wiki.text: Mulberry Group PLC is a British fashion company founded in 1971, best known for its luxury leather goods, particularly women's handbags.

about: Rothy's is a San Francisco direct-to-consumer footwear and accessories brand, founded in 2012, known for washable shoes and bags knitted from recycled plastic bottles and marine plastic. It sells flats, sneakers, sandals and handbags online and through its own stores in the US and in international markets. It has raised about $519 million and became a fashion brand with a loyal following of women. Strong consumer brand in the US, with a sustainability image.

wiki.title: Rothy's
wiki.text: Rothy's is an American direct-to-consumer company which designs and sells shoes and accessories. Rothy's was initially founded in 2012 and launched in 2016 by Stephen Hawthornthwaite and Roth Martin as a women's shoe company in San Francisco. It has since expanded with handbags and a men's line.

wiki.title: Patagonia
wiki.text: Patagonia is a geographical region that encompasses the southern end of South America, governed by Argentina and Chile. The region comprises the southern section of the Andes mountains, featuring lakes, fjords, temperate rainforests, and glaciers in the west, and deserts, tablelands, and steppes to the east. Patagonia is bounded by the Pacific Ocean on the west, the Atlantic Ocean to the east, and many bodies of water that connect them, including the Strait of Magellan, the Beagle Channel, and the Drake Passage to the south.

wiki.title: Patagonia, Inc.
wiki.text: Patagonia, Inc. is an American retailer of outdoor recreation clothing, equipment, and food. It was founded by Yvon Chouinard in 1973 and is based in Ventura, California. Patagonia operates stores in over ten countries, and factories in sixteen countries.

about: RxSight is an Aliso Viejo, California medical device company listed on Nasdaq (RXST), maker of the Light Adjustable Lens, an intraocular lens for cataract patients that can be tuned after surgery with a light delivery device. Customers are ophthalmologists and surgery centres. Revenue is over $150 million and growing. B2B medical technology with limited consumer awareness.

Bombas is a US direct-to-consumer apparel brand, started in 2013 by David Heath and Randy Goldberg, best known for comfort-focused socks, and now also underwear, t-shirts, slippers and sweaters. For every item sold it donates one to homeless shelters and community organisations, with well over 100 million items given. It sells mainly online and through selected retailers. Based in New York, it has raised about $150 million and is privately held. Strong consumer awareness in the US, driven by heavy digital marketing.

wiki.title: Bombas
wiki.text: Bombas is an American apparel brand. The company is known mainly for their socks, but has since expanded into other clothing categories. The majority of its sales are made direct-to-consumer, augmented by a small percentage from wholesale partners. For every item purchased, a clothing item is donated to a homeless shelter or homelessness-related charity.

about: Versace is an Italian luxury fashion house, based in Milan, founded by Gianni Versace in 1978, selling ready-to-wear, accessories, fragrances, eyewear, jewellery and home products through boutiques, department stores and online. Its Medusa logo is globally known. Customers are affluent consumers worldwide. Owned by Capri Holdings since 2018, when it was bought for $2.1 billion, it was in turn sold to Prada Group in a deal announced in April 2025 for about EUR 1.25 billion. Very well-known global luxury brand.
flags: last funding 2014: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: Versace
wiki.what: Italian luxury fashion house in Milan
wiki.text: Gianni Versace S.r.l., usually referred to as Versace, is an Italian luxury elite fashion company founded by Gianni Versace in 1978. It produces Italian-made ready-to-wear and accessories, as well as haute couture under its Atelier Versace brand and licenses its name and branding to Luxottica for eyewear.

about: Bira 91 is an Indian craft beer brand, from B9 Beverages, based in New Delhi, selling Bira 91 White Ale, Blonde, and other beers through retail and taprooms in India and exports. Founded in 2015 by Ankur Jain, it expanded fast but suffered losses and a funding crunch from 2023, with leadership changes. It has raised about $318 million. Known to young Indian drinkers, with notable presence in cricket and music events.

wiki.title: Bira 91
wiki.text: Bira 91 is an Indian craft beer brand manufactured by B9 Beverages Pvt. Ltd., launched in 2015. Made from wheat, barley and hops, the beer is available in draft, 330ml, 650ml bottles and 500ml cans.

about: Gong cha is an international bubble tea franchise, originating in Taiwan in 2006 and run from London, selling milk teas, fruit teas and toppings through franchised shops in about 25 countries, with well over 2,000 stores. Customers are mostly younger consumers, and it earns franchise fees and product sales to franchisees. It has changed hands among private equity owners, with Crunchbase showing about $200 million raised around 2019. Strong youth-oriented consumer brand in Asia, Australia, the UK and the US.

India's largest wine producer, based in Nashik, Maharashtra. Brands include Sula, Rasa, Dindori, The Source and Madera, and it runs vineyard resorts and tasting rooms that make it a leader in Indian wine tourism. It sells to consumers and hospitality across India with exports to over 20 countries, and monetises through wine sales and wine tourism. Founded in 1999 by Rajeev Samant, it listed on the NSE and BSE in December 2022 (SULA). Recognised consumer alcohol brand in India with an events and festival presence (SulaFest).

wiki.title: Sula Vineyards
wiki.what: Winery and vineyard in Nashik, India
wiki.text: Sula Vineyards is a winery and vineyard located in the Nashik region of western India, approximately 180 kilometres (110 mi) northeast of Mumbai. It was founded by Rajeev Samant in 1999. Sula has grown to be India's largest and most awarded wine brand. Sula introduced grape varietals such as Chenin blanc, Sauvignon blanc, Riesling and Zinfandel in India and is the leading player in the Indian wine industry.

about: Drinks manufacturer, marketer and distributor with a portfolio of cider and beer brands including Bulmers (in Ireland), Magners, Tennent's lager and Menabrea, plus an on-trade distribution arm serving pubs, restaurants and hotels across the UK and Ireland. Revenue comes from alcohol sales and wholesale distribution, with annual sales well over one billion euros. Headquartered in Glasgow with roots in Ireland, it is listed in Dublin and London (CCR). Customers are pubs, retailers and consumers; brand visibility is high in Britain and Ireland, with a long history of sport and festival sponsorship.

wiki.title: C&C Group
wiki.text: C&C Group plc is an Irish manufacturer, marketer and distributor of alcoholic drinks, particularly cider, and soft drinks. It has production facilities across Ireland, Great Britain and the United States, and its products are sold around the world. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange.

about: Switzerland-based world's largest chocolate and cocoa product maker, supplying industrial and artisan chocolatiers, bakeries, food manufacturers and restaurants with chocolate, cocoa and fillings under Callebaut, Cacao Barry and Van Houten. Revenue near 8 billion Swiss francs and about 13,000 employees in over 30 countries. Headquartered in Zurich; formed in 1996. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (BARN), with Jacobs Holding and Renata Coray related interests. B2B ingredient supplier with limited consumer brand awareness, though its brands are professional favourites.

wiki.title: Barry Callebaut
wiki.text: Barry Callebaut AG is a Swiss-Belgian cocoa processor and chocolate manufacturer. It was created in 1996 through the merging of the French company Cacao Barry and the Belgian chocolate producer Callebaut, and it is based in Zürich, Switzerland. The company was created in its present form by Klaus Johann Jacobs. In 2019, it had 61 production sites, located in Europe, Africa, the Americas, and Asia.

about: US food company known for Greek yogurt, also selling oat milk, creamers, coffee drinks, kefir and probiotics. Founded in 2005 by Hamdi Ulukaya, with its largest facilities in New Berlin, New York and Twin Falls, Idaho, and revenue near 3 billion dollars plus. Sells through supermarkets across the US and abroad. Privately held, with TPG and others as investors; raised large capital in 2025 at a valuation of 20 billion dollars. Strong consumer brand and a sponsor of US Olympic and Paralympic teams.

wiki.title: Chobani
wiki.text: Chobani is an American food company specializing in strained yogurt. The company was founded in 2005 by Hamdi Ulukaya. Chobani sells thick, Greek yogurt with a higher protein content than traditional yogurt and is one of the main companies to popularize this style of yogurt in the US. The company has also expanded to non-dairy, plant-based products such as dairy-free vegan yogurt and oat milk. Chobani produces a variety of Greek yogurt products, oat drinks, and snacks. Chobani's yogurt market share in the U.S. rose from less than 1% in 2007 to more than 20% in 2021, and is the top-selling Greek yogurt brand in the United States and operates t

about: World's largest meat company, processing beef, pork, chicken and lamb and selling under Seara, Swift, Friboi, Pilgrim's Pride, Moy Park and Primo Foods brands as well as plant-based Vivera. Customers are retailers, food service and consumers in over 190 countries, with revenue near 70 to 80 billion dollars. Headquartered in Sao Paulo, Brazil; founded 1953 by the Batista family, who control it. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange (JBS) in 2025, with a Brazilian listing too. Mostly B2B, with consumer brands in some markets, and a past sponsor of football and sports.

Olam Food Ingredients is the food and beverage ingredients business of Olam Group, supplying cocoa, coffee, dairy, nuts and spices to food manufacturers and retailers. Customers are food and beverage producers worldwide, with the coffee and cocoa lines among the largest globally. Headquartered in Singapore; Olam Group is majority owned by Singapore's Temasek. ofi was set up in 2022 as a separate business within Olam and has been preparing for a separate listing. B2B ingredient supplier with limited consumer awareness.
cb_desc: ofisa naturally beneficial ingredients and solutions for...

about: Guala Closures is an Italian maker of aluminium and plastic closures for spirits, wine, water, beverage and oil bottles, including tamper-evident and anti-counterfeiting designs. Customers are global drinks groups. Operates plants in about 30 countries. Headquartered in Spinetta Marengo, Piedmont; founded 1954. Taken private by Investindustrial in 2018 after its 2007 listing. B2B packaging supplier with no consumer awareness.

Haldiram's Snacks is the Noida, Uttar Pradesh-based Indian snack food company behind Haldiram's bhujia, namkeen, sweets, ready-to-eat meals and packaged foods, sold through retail in India and exported to dozens of countries. It is a family-founded group with Bikaner, Nagpur and Delhi entities. In 2025 Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Alpha Wave and Temasek bought minority stakes valuing it at around $10bn. Private. Beloved Indian consumer brand with big advertising reach.

wiki.title: Haldiram's
wiki.what: Vegetarian Indian restaurant and foodstuff manufacturer
wiki.text: Haldiram's India Pvt Ltd, doing business as Haldiram's is an Indian multinational fast-food restaurant chain, founded in 1937, as a confectionery and desserts shop in Bikaner, Rajasthan, by Ganga Bhishen Agarwal. It is currently based in Nagpur, Maharashtra. Haldiram's is also a FMCG company as most of its restaurants have a integrated retail section, where packaged Indian snacks and confectioneries are sold under its own brand.

about: Hershey is a Pennsylvania-based confectionery and snack company founded in 1894, making Hershey's chocolate, Reese's, Kisses, Kit Kat (US license), Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, plus salty snacks such as SkinnyPop and Dot's Pretzels. Customers are consumers via grocery, mass retailers and convenience stores, mainly in North America, with sales of about $11 billion. Listed on NYSE (HSY), controlled by the Hershey Trust. Household-name consumer brand with heavy marketing.

JDE Peet's is an Amsterdam-based global coffee and tea company, created by the 2020 merger of Jacobs Douwe Egberts and Peet's Coffee. Brands include Douwe Egberts, Jacobs, L'OR, Tassimo, Senseo, Peet's and Pickwick, sold in more than 100 markets with revenue of roughly 9 billion euros. Customers are consumers via retailers and foodservice. Controlled by JAB Holding and listed on Euronext Amsterdam from 2020; Keurig Dr Pepper agreed to acquire it in 2025. Well-known grocery brands in Europe.

Jersey Mike's Subs is a Manasquan, New Jersey sub sandwich franchisor founded in 1956, with about 3,000 restaurants in the US, and sales of over $3 billion. Customers are consumers buying sandwiches in-store and online. Blackstone acquired it in 2024 in a deal valuing it at about $8 billion; the input shows reported funding of $760 million. Strong US consumer brand, a sponsor of sports including NASCAR and the Jersey Mike's 400.

wiki.title: Jersey Mike's Subs
wiki.text: Jersey Mike’s Subs Inc., is an American multinational submarine sandwich chain headquartered in Manasquan, New Jersey. The Jersey Mike's franchise has about 3,000 locations, with locations in the United States, Canada, and elsewhere.

about: Italian tomato and prepared foods producer, based in Angri, Campania, supplying canned tomato products, beverages and sauces to retailers across Europe, with a large UK trade. B2B and private label with limited consumer recognition. Sells canned tomatoes, pasta sauces, fruit juices and fruit-based drinks for retailers and private label across Europe. Founded 1954. Low consumer recognition. La Doria is among the leading Italian suppliers of canned tomato products to British supermarkets.

Tempe, Arizona-based drive-through coffee chain, Dutch Bros, founded 1992 in Oregon, with over 1,000 shops across the US. Listed on the NYSE (BROS). Revenue about $1.5 billion. Strong regional consumer brand, expanding nationally. The chain has over 1,000 locations, mainly in the western US, and is expanding eastward. Revenue is about $1.5 billion. Dutch Bros also sells energy drinks, teas and smoothies, and draws strong loyalty from regular customers.

wiki.title: Dutch Bros Coffee
wiki.text: Dutch Bros Inc., originally written Dutch Bros., is a publicly held drive-through coffee chain in the United States. Founded in 1992 by Dane and Travis Boersma, it is headquartered in Tempe, Arizona, after having been based in Grants Pass, Oregon, for many years prior to 2025. It has company-owned and franchise locations primarily located in the Western United States, although the company has expanded as far east as Orlando, Florida.

about: San Miguel Corporation is the Philippines' largest conglomerate by sales, founded in 1890 and based in Mandaluyong, with businesses in food and beverage (San Miguel Beer, Ginebra San Miguel, Magnolia), packaging, energy (Meralco stake, power plants), infrastructure (airports, tollways) and fuel retail. Controlled by the Ramon Ang-led group, and listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (SMC). Revenue is around 1.4 trillion pesos. San Miguel Beer is a household brand with heavy sports sponsorship, including basketball.

Impossible Foods is a Redwood City, California food company, founded in 2011, that makes plant-based meat products such as the Impossible Burger, sausage and nuggets, using a soy leghemoglobin ingredient. It sells through supermarkets and restaurant chains such as Burger King, and operates in the US, Canada, Asia and Europe. Funding is about $1.9 billion from investors including Khosla and Temasek. Strong consumer brand in plant-based food, and has previously sponsored sport.

wiki.title: Impossible Foods
wiki.text: Impossible Foods Inc. is a company that develops plant-based substitutes for meat products. The company's signature product, the Impossible Burger, was launched in July 2016 as a vegan alternative to a beef hamburger.

about: Toast is a Boston-based restaurant technology company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TOST), which sells cloud-based point-of-sale systems, payments, payroll, online ordering and delivery tools to over 130,000 restaurant locations, mainly in the US. It earns subscriptions and payment fees, with revenue of about $5 billion. Known among restaurateurs, and has sponsored sports properties such as Boston teams.

The Manitowoc Company is a Milwaukee, Wisconsin maker of cranes, selling Grove mobile cranes, Manitowoc crawler and tower cranes and Potain tower cranes, after spinning off foodservice equipment business as Welbilt in 2016. Customers are construction and infrastructure contractors and rental companies worldwide. It is listed on the NYSE (MTW) with revenue of about 2 billion dollars. It is a B2B industrial brand, well known on construction sites but not to consumers.

wiki.title: The Manitowoc Company
wiki.text: The Manitowoc Company, Inc. is an American manufacturer which produces cranes and previously produced commercial refrigeration and marine equipment. It was founded in 1902 and, through its wholly owned subsidiaries, designs, manufactures, markets, and supports mobile telescopic cranes, tower cranes, lattice-boom crawler cranes, and boom trucks under the Grove, Manitowoc, National Crane, Potain, Shuttlelift and Manitowoc Crane Care brand names.

about: Liquid Death is a Los Angeles based canned water and beverage brand, sold as mountain water, sparkling water and iced tea in tallboy cans with a heavy-metal, anti-plastic identity. Founded by Mike Cessario in 2017, it is sold in major US retailers, Whole Foods, Target and convenience stores, and in the UK, and has expanded into merchandise and brand collaborations. It was valued at 1.4 billion dollars in 2024 after raising about $268 million. It is a hugely visible consumer brand.

wiki.title: Liquid Death
wiki.text: Supplying Demand, Inc., doing business as Liquid Death, is a canned water company founded by Mike Cessario, headquartered in Los Angeles, California, United States. Its tagline is "murder your thirst". The drink is sold in a 12 US fl oz (350 ml), 16.9 US fl oz (500 ml) "tallboy" drink can and a 19.2 US fl oz (570 ml) can. As of 2023, its water was canned by Wilderness Asset Holdings LLC in Virginia, US. The drink began selling to consumers on its website in January 2019. In March 2024, the company was valued at $1.4 billion. Liquid Death currently has 14 flavors.

about: Cipriani is a luxury Italian hospitality brand founded in Venice around Harry's Bar by Giuseppe Cipriani in 1931, now run by the Cipriani family, with restaurants, event venues and clubs in New York, Miami, London, Dubai, Hong Kong and elsewhere, as well as a food products line. The US business is based in New York and the group produces high-end dining and events. Its Crunchbase funding is about $190 million. It is a prestigious restaurant and events brand with strong awareness among affluent consumers.

Blank Street is a New York coffee chain founded in 2020 in Brooklyn, with small-format cafes and kiosks serving espresso drinks and matcha at lower prices, with roughly 100 or more locations in New York, Boston, Washington, London and other cities. Customers are urban consumers. It has raised about $255 million in venture funding. Growing consumer brand in big-city markets, popular on social media.

Thai seafood group based in Bangkok, listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (TU), owning canned tuna brands such as Chicken of the Sea, John West and Petit Navire, plus pet food and value-added ingredients. Sells in over 100 countries. Revenue around 140 billion baht. Strong consumer brand in Europe and North America.

wiki.title: Thai Union Group
wiki.text: Thai Union Group PCL is a Thailand-based producer of seafood based products. It was founded in 1977, and was listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) on 22 November 1994.

about: Eat Just is a San Francisco-based food technology company that makes plant-based egg (JUST Egg) from mung beans and cultivated meat under the Good Meat brand. Founded in 2011 as Hampton Creek, it has raised about $465 million and sells in grocery stores in the US and abroad. Consumer brand with strong visibility in plant-based food, though not a household name.

wiki.title: Eat Just
wiki.text: Eat Just Food Company is a private company headquartered in San Francisco, California, US. It develops and markets plant-based alternatives to conventionally produced egg products, as well as cultivated meat products. Eat Just was founded in 2011 by Josh Tetrick and Josh Balk. It raised about $120 million in early venture capital and became a unicorn in 2016 by surpassing a $1 billion valuation. It has been involved in several highly publicized disputes with traditional egg industry interests. In December 2020, its cultivated chicken nugget product became the first cultured meat to receive regulatory approval in the world, following its appro

about: Cloetta is a Stockholm-based Swedish confectionery company, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (CLA B), maker of Läkerol, Jolly Rancher (licensed in Europe), Malaco, Cloetta Chocolate, Ahlgrens bilar and Kexchoklad brands. Its sweets are sold across the Nordics and Europe, with annual revenue of about SEK 8 billion. Strong consumer brand in Nordic countries.

wiki.title: Cloetta
wiki.text: Cloetta AB is a Swedish confectionery company. The company manufactures and sells local confectionery brands on its main markets Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, Netherlands, Germany and the UK.

about: Laird Superfood is a plant-based food company founded by big-wave surfer Laird Hamilton and partners, selling creamers, coffee, superfood powders and snacks, based in the US and listed on NYSE American (LSF). It sells through grocery, online and wholesale channels. Revenue is small, in the tens of millions of dollars. A niche health-food brand with moderate US awareness.

LifeMD is a New York telehealth company listed on Nasdaq (LFMD) that offers virtual care for weight management, men's and women's health, dermatology and primary care, under brands including RexMD and WorkSimpli. It sells subscriptions and prescriptions to consumers in the US, with revenue of about $200 million. A direct-to-consumer health brand with heavy digital advertising, and moderate awareness.

wiki.title: LifeMD
wiki.text: LifeMD, Inc. is a publicly traded American telehealth company. It gives subscribers access to doctors and nurse practitioners for virtual medical consultations and treatments with prescription medications.

about: Califia Farms is a Los Angeles, California natural beverage company known for plant-based milks and coffee drinks, including almond, oat, coconut and cold brew products, sold in refrigerated grocery sections in the US and Canada. Customers are mainly health-conscious consumers through retailers such as Target and Whole Foods. Founded in 2010, it has raised about 340 million dollars from investors including Sun Capital and Temasek. It is private. A well-recognized US premium plant milk brand with its distinctive bottle.

Potbelly Sandwich Works is a US fast-casual sandwich chain headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. It serves toasted sandwiches, salads, soups and milkshakes in roughly 450 shops, mostly company-owned plus franchised stores across the US, with delivery and catering. Founded in 1977, it earns money from food sales and franchise fees. It is listed on Nasdaq (PBPB). Recognisable consumer restaurant brand with regional strength in the Midwest and with moderate national awareness.

wiki.title: Potbelly Sandwich Shop
wiki.text: Potbelly Sandwich Shop, also known as Potbelly Sandwich Works, is an American fast-casual restaurant chain with over 400 locations that focuses on submarine sandwiches and milkshakes. It is owned by RaceTrac.

about: Vita Coco is a New York-based coconut water company, selling Vita Coco coconut water in cartons and bottles, plus coconut oil, Runa tea and the Ever & Ever and PWR LIFT brands. It sources coconuts from the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Brazil and elsewhere, and sells through grocery, convenience and club retailers in the US and about 40 other countries, with annual revenue of roughly 500 million dollars. Founded in 2004, it is listed on Nasdaq (COCO). Widely recognised consumer beverage brand with a history of celebrity and sports sponsorship.

DailyPay is a US financial technology company that lets employees access earned wages before payday through an employer-integrated app, using a model funded by employers and optional employee fees. Customers are large employers in retail, hospitality, healthcare and logistics, and their staff, with millions of users. Founded in 2015 and based in New York, it has raised well over $1 billion in equity and debt. B2B2C brand known among hourly workers.

wiki.title: DailyPay
wiki.text: DailyPay is an American technology company founded in 2015, which provides payroll services such as on-demand pay.

about: Alera Group is a Deerfield, Illinois-based insurance brokerage and financial services firm, offering employee benefits, property and casualty, retirement plan, wealth management and consulting services to businesses and individuals through acquired local agencies across the US. Backed by private equity investors, including Stone Point Capital, with growth through frequent acquisitions. Revenue is about $1 billion or more. Mainly B2B, with some local consumer exposure but little national brand awareness.
cb_desc: Alera Group is a financial services firm specializing in...

about: HiBob is a New York- and Tel Aviv-based human resources platform for mid-size companies, with its Bob product handling core HR, payroll, performance and benefits. Founded in 2015 by Ronni Zehavi, it has raised about $740 million and is valued at $2.45 billion. Customers include many fast-growing companies. B2B software, known in HR tech.
cb_desc: HiBob is a people management platform that offers benefit...

wiki.title: HiBob
wiki.text: HiBob is a human resources software company that develops Bob, a cloud-based human capital management platform. The company was founded in Tel Aviv in 2015 by Amit Knaani, Ronni Zehavi, Israel David, and Andy Bellass, and is headquartered in London. HiBob has raised several rounds of venture funding, including a US$150 million Series C in 2021 and a US$150 million funding round in 2023 that valued the company at nearly US$2.7 billion.The company expanded its platform through the acquisitions of payroll automation company Pento in 2024 and financial planning and analysis platform Mosaic in 2025.

about: TriNet is a US professional employer organisation based in Dublin, California, providing outsourced HR services, payroll, benefits, insurance and compliance to small and mid-sized businesses, often in technology, financial services, healthcare and professional services. It serves several hundred thousand worksite employees and generates annual revenue of a few billion dollars, listed on the NYSE as TNET. Founded in 1988. B2B, with moderate brand awareness among small-business owners but none among consumers.

wiki.title: TriNet
wiki.text: TriNet Group, Inc. is a professional employer organization for small and medium-sized businesses. TriNet administers payroll and health benefits and advises clients on employment law compliance and risk reduction, acting in some cases as an outsourced human resources department. TriNet is headquartered in Dublin, California. TriNet partners with organizations between 3 and 2,500 employees.

about: Asure Software is an Austin-based provider of cloud human capital management software, including payroll, tax, time and attendance, HR and benefits administration for small and mid-sized businesses, sold across the US. Listed on Nasdaq (ASUR). Revenue is about 120 million dollars. Funding of 177 million dollars recorded. Customers are employers who pay subscriptions. B2B software vendor with moderate brand visibility among small businesses.

wiki.title: Asure Software
wiki.text: Asure Software, Inc. is a software company. Prior to September 13, 2007, the company was known as Forgent Networks. After rebranding as Asure Software, the company expanded into offering human capital management (HCM) solutions, including payroll, time & attendance, talent management, human resource management, benefits administration and insurance services.

about: Personio is a Munich-based human resources software company that offers an all-in-one cloud platform for small and mid-size European companies, covering recruiting, payroll, absence and employee data. Founded in 2015, it raised about $720 million and reached a valuation of $8.5 billion in 2021. Customers are SMEs across Germany, Spain, France and the UK, who pay subscriptions. It is a B2B brand well known among European HR professionals and an active marketing sponsor, though not a household name.

wiki.title: Personio
wiki.text: Personio is a European software company headquartered in Munich, Germany that develops cloud-based human resource management software for small and medium-sized businesses operating internationally.

about: First Advantage is an Atlanta-area background screening and workforce identity company providing employment verification, criminal checks, drug screening and onboarding technology for employers. It is listed on Nasdaq (FA), and merged with Sterling Check in 2024. Customers are large employers across many industries. It is a B2B human resources technology brand with no consumer profile, although its name appears in job application processes.
